key_insight: BRIDGE treats retrieval and policy learning as a bilevel problem to fix the credit-assignment gap in agentic RL, showing that improving retrieval first can unlock larger downstream reasoning gains.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical way to jointly train retrievers and LLM agents for knowledge-intensive systems, improving accuracy on multi-hop and medical QA without sacrificing efficiency.
method: Formulates retrieval-augmented agentic reinforcement learning as a bilevel optimization problem.
Uses a memory-efficient first-order bilevel algorithm to co-adapt retriever and LLM policy.
Motivated by loss-landscape analysis to preserve the order-sensitive advantage of retrieval before policy updates.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on seven open-domain QA benchmarks, BRIDGE achieved the best average accuracy with 3B and 7B backbones, including multi-hop gains of 9.6 EM and 3.4 EM over the strongest baseline.
watch_item: Because performance depends on bilevel training stability and the quality of retrieved evidence, deployment may be sensitive to retriever choice, optimization hyperparameters, and compute budget.
paper_title: BRIDGE: Bilevel Retrieval-Credit-Aware Agentic Reinforcement Learning
